context: A senior trains a new hire on summarizing reports
purpose: Teach: 展望/要約/謝罪/かかわる/生み出し/係る/もたらし/行なっ

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: じゃあ今日は報告書の要約のやり方を教えるね。これ、仕事の質にかかわる大事なスキルだから。
lines.en: Okay, today I'll teach you how to summarize reports. This is a skill that affects the quality of your work.
lines.style: Warm mentoring tone with gentle authority and patience

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、よろしくお願いします。大学のレポートとは違う感じですよね?
lines.en: Yes, please teach me. It's different from university reports, right?
lines.style: Eager polite junior voice slightly nervous and attentive

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 全然違うよ。まず冒頭に結論、それから事業に係る数字、最後に今後の展望を入れる。この三点セットね。
lines.en: Totally different. First the conclusion at the top, then the numbers related to the business, and finally the future outlook. That's the three-point set.
lines.style: Crisp instructive delivery with structured business clarity

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。先週うちの部署が大きな成果を生み出していましたが、ああいう実績はどう書けば?
lines.en: I see. Our department produced big results last week — how should I write up that kind of achievement?
lines.style: Curious applied learner referencing concrete recent example

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 数字で示すのが一番。「新規契約を二十件獲得し、売上に大きな変化をもたらしました」みたいに具体的に書く。
lines.en: Numbers are the most convincing. Write concretely, like 'we secured twenty new contracts, bringing significant change to sales.'
lines.style: Practical example-driven coaching with concrete phrasing

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: あの、もし数字にミスがあったらどうするんですか?やっぱり謝罪のメールとか…
lines.en: Um, what if there's a mistake in the numbers? Should I send an apology email or something?
lines.style: Hesitant worried junior raising a real concern

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: ミスは誰でもする。先月も私、訂正を行なって部長に頭を下げたよ。隠さず早めに報告するのが鉄則。
lines.en: Everyone makes mistakes. Last month I issued a correction and bowed to the manager myself. The iron rule is to report early, never hide it.
lines.style: Reassuring honest senior sharing personal vulnerability

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 先輩でもそういうことが…ちょっと安心しました。じゃあ早速一本書いてみます。
lines.en: Even you've had that happen... I feel a bit relieved. Then I'll try writing one right away.
lines.style: Relieved motivated tone with renewed confidence

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: うん、書けたら見せて。最初は完璧じゃなくていい。場数を踏むことが成長にもたらす効果は大きいから。
lines.en: Yes, show me when it's done. It doesn't have to be perfect at first. Gaining experience has a huge effect on growth.
lines.style: Encouraging closing with patient long-view perspective
